Apixaban for the treatment of venous thromboembolism: eight trials report an outcome named for recurrent VTE, and three of them count the same thing

In adults with acute or recent venous thromboembolism, what is the effect of apixaban compared with conventional anticoagulation, another direct oral anticoagulant, or placebo on recurrent venous thromboembolism and on bleeding?

In this section: Registration and administrative information (PROSPERO field set)

Registration and administrative information (PROSPERO field set)

Table 1. Registration and administrative information (PROSPERO field set)
Review titleApixaban for the treatment of venous thromboembolism: eight trials report an outcome named for recurrent VTE, and three of them count the same thing
Review question (PICO)In adults with acute or recent venous thromboembolism, what is the effect of apixaban compared with conventional anticoagulation, another direct oral anticoagulant, or placebo on recurrent venous thromboembolism and on bleeding?
Background / rationaleNot recorded — this object holds no background field, and an introduction generated without one would be argument that no source in this review supports
Eligibility criteriaPOPULATION: adults with acute or recent venous thromboembolism being TREATED for it. INTERVENTION: apixaban as the randomised intervention -- the drug itself, not a class of which it is one member. COMPARATOR: conventional anticoagulation, another direct oral anticoagulant, or placebo. ESTIMAND, which governs POOLABILITY and not eligibility: recurrent venous thromboembolism, or major bleeding, at ANY registered rank. AND THE BOUNDARY WITH THE PROPHYLAXIS REVIEW: extended anticoagulation in patients who have ALREADY HAD a venous thromboembolism is TREATMENT and belongs here; primary prophylaxis in patients who have not is PREVENTION and belongs to the sibling. The discriminator is read from each trial's eligibility criteria, because the registry's coded `primaryPurpose` does not carry it and both conventions are used for both situations. Criteria are DERIVED POST HOC and say so.
Information sources0 source layers, listed on the Extraction tab
Search strategyThe executed strings, datetimes, filters and hit counts are on the Search tab
Study selection processTwo independent screeners of different model families, title/abstract then full text, with named human adjudication
Number of screenersTwo, cross-family. Two instances of one model is one screener run twice and its agreement statistic is meaningless
Data extraction itemsRegistry id, primary publication, year, design, population, arms, the analysed denominator and the randomised total SEPARATELY, per-arm event counts, and the published effect with its interval and its stated level
Outcomes and prioritisationRecurrent symptomatic venous thromboembolism -- nonfatal deep vein thrombosis or nonfatal pulmonary embolism -- with NO death term
Risk of bias methodNot recorded — no per-domain RoB-2 assessment exists yet
Synthesis methodsRandom effects on the log scale; REML headline; HKSJ reported alongside; leave-one-out and an estimator comparison, all pre-specified before the search
Subgroup analysesNot recorded — none pre-specified. At this k any contrast would be underpowered and post hoc, and none will later be presented as though planned
Meta-bias assessmentFunnel, Egger and Peters, each reported as a computed value with the caveat that below about ten studies they have almost no power
Certainty assessmentGRADE, all five domains, on the Certainty tab
Confidence level95%
FundingNot recorded — no funding statement is recorded for this review
Competing interestsNot recorded — no declaration is recorded

Pooled result

RR 0.7763 (0.3437 to 1.753), 95% interval

Recurrent symptomatic venous thromboembolism -- nonfatal deep vein thrombosis or nonfatal pulmonary embolism -- with NO death term. random-effects, estimator REML, k = 3.

τ² 0 · I² 0% · Q 1.257 on 2 df

Favours: neither -- the interval spans the null

computed; tau-squared is 0 and at k=3 that is an estimate from almost no information, which is why the interval is Knapp-Hartung on 2 degrees of freedom rather than a normal one

Three trials randomise apixaban ITSELF against another anticoagulant for the acute event and post an arm-level count of recurrent symptomatic VTE with no death term. Their definitions were read and compared, not their names.

READ THIS BESIDE THE ESTIMATE. NOT ONE of the three contributing trials masks anybody: NCT03045406, NCT03266783 and NCT01780987 all register MASKING: NONE. The endpoint is adjudicated on all three, which is the standard mitigation for an open-label anticoagulation trial, but NO REGISTRATION STATES THAT THE ADJUDICATORS WERE BLINDED.

On NCT03266783 the registered primary is CLINICALLY RELEVANT BLEEDING and recurrent VTE is the third of nine secondaries. On NCT01780987 the registered primary is MAJOR BLEEDING and recurrent VTE is the first of five. ONLY CARAVAGGIO CONTRIBUTES ITS OWN REGISTERED PRIMARY.

Dalteparin, rivaroxaban, and unfractionated heparin followed by warfarin. The pooled quantity is therefore apixaban against WHATEVER ELSE WAS GIVEN, which is one step from any question a reader has. This object's GRADE rates indirectness down for it and the certainty here is VERY LOW.

THE DEATH TERM IS PART OF THE DEFINITION AND NOT A DETAIL. Five of the eleven trials register a primary composite carrying one, and they do not carry the SAME one: AMPLIFY counts VTE-related death, AMPLIFY-EXT counts ALL-CAUSE death. Same sponsor, same programme, sequential trials, names differing by a hyphenated suffix.

Leave-one-out sensitivity

Does the reported estimate depend on any one of the three trials? At k=3 that is not a formality: the largest contributor is more than seven times the size of the other two together.

Table 10. Leave-one-out sensitivity
Cohort omittedkRR (95% CI)
CARAVAGGIO21.021 (0.0105 to 99.38)
COBRRA20.6904 (0.0419 to 11.37)
Japanese acute DVT/PE study20.7859 (0.0681 to 9.069)

AT k=3 THE POOL IS LARGELY ONE TRIAL. CARAVAGGIO contributes 78 of the 108 events in this pool; its two companions contribute 30 between them. Omitting it moves the point estimate from 0.776 to 1.021, and the span across all three leave-one-out fits is 0.690 to 1.021. All three intervals span the null, so no single trial is holding the conclusion up -- and none is holding it down either. The honest reading is that this estimate is a description of CARAVAGGIO with two small trials attached.

Cochrane Handbook 10.14: sensitivity analyses ask whether the conclusions are robust to decisions made during the review. Here the decision under test is the inclusion of each individual trial, not the estimator -- the estimator comparison is reported separately at `estimator_sensitivity`, because they are different questions and presenting them in one table would let a stable point estimate under one read as stability under the other.

Projected from the canonical object, so it carries the same k, the same pooled estimate and the same interval as the paper and cannot drift from them. The interval is drawn CROSSING the no-difference line because it does: a graphical abstract travels without its caption, and one that showed a favourable point estimate without showing that its interval includes no effect would be overstating a null result, which is a defect class this review documents in other papers.

Title and review question

Apixaban for the treatment of venous thromboembolism: eight trials report an outcome named for recurrent VTE, and three of them count the same thing1

In adults with acute or recent venous thromboembolism, what is the effect of apixaban compared with conventional anticoagulation, another direct oral anticoagulant, or placebo on recurrent venous thromboembolism and on bleeding?2

Abstract

Question. In adults with acute or recent venous thromboembolism, what is the effect of apixaban compared with conventional anticoagulation, another direct oral anticoagulant, or placebo on recurrent venous thromboembolism and on bleeding?1

Methods. ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 and PubMed (ncbi e-utilities esearch) were searched; estimates were pooled under a random-effects with the REML estimator; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials); and certainty was rated with GRADE.2

Results. Recurrent symptomatic venous thromboembolism -- nonfatal deep vein thrombosis or nonfatal pulmonary embolism -- with NO death term: risk ratio 0.776 (0.344 to 1.75) across 3 trials; 1 of these pooled outcome(s) carries a stated qualification -- a referral or a recorded finding -- given in full in Results and not reproduced here; the trials agreed closely (I-squared 0%); and certainty of the evidence was very low.3

Refused: the Background sentence of the abstract. Background is argument -- why this question matters -- and no arrangement of the quantities this object holds yields it. It is emitted only from an authored field and there is no composition path for it here4
Refused: the Conclusions sentence of the abstract. A conclusion is argument -- what a reader should now believe -- and it is emitted only from an authored field. Composing one from the estimate would be this renderer telling the reader what to conclude, which no field supports5

Introduction

1Background. This review asks: In adults with acute or recent venous thromboembolism, what is the effect of apixaban compared with conventional anticoagulation, another direct oral anticoagulant, or placebo on recurrent venous thromboembolism and on bleeding? It pools 3 randomised trials, against another anticoagulant. The outcome pooled is Recurrent symptomatic venous thromboembolism -- nonfatal deep vein thrombosis or nonfatal pulmonary embolism -- with NO death term.

[Draft] The evidence identified on this question is 3 randomised trials (NCT01780987, NCT03045406, NCT03266783), pooled here at 0.776 (95% CI 0.344 to 1.753) for recurrent_vte. Certainty in that estimate is rated VERY_LOW. Which of those unresolved points makes the question worth asking now is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] No search for published syntheses is recorded on this object. Whether those differences warrant a new synthesis rather than citing the existing one is the author's judgement.3

Methods — search

Searches were executed in ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 on 2026-08-19 with the query, verbatim: Executed 2026-08-19 against ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, raw. query.cond="venous thromboembolism OR deep vein thrombosis OR pulmonary embolism"; query.intr="apixaban"; filter.advanced=AREA[StudyType]INTERVENTIONAL -- NO PHASE FILTER. 82 records, returned == totalCount, nextPageToken null.. It returned 82 record(s).1

Searches were executed in ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 -- FIRST QUERY, RECORDED BECAUSE IT MISSED on 2026-08-19 with the query, verbatim: same terms with filter.advanced=... AND AREA[Phase](PHASE3 OR PHASE4). It returned 49 record(s).2

Searches were executed in PubMed (NCBI E-utilities esearch) on 2026-08-19 with the query, verbatim: apixaban AND venous thromboembolism. It returned 50 record(s).3

Primary trials. No bibliographic search for primary trials was run. The 4 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on the dates recorded on each entry.4

Methods — eligibility criteria

POPULATION: adults with acute or recent venous thromboembolism being TREATED for it. INTERVENTION: apixaban as the randomised intervention -- the drug itself, not a class of which it is one member. COMPARATOR: conventional anticoagulation, another direct oral anticoagulant, or placebo. ESTIMAND, which governs POOLABILITY and not eligibility: recurrent venous thromboembolism, or major bleeding, at ANY registered rank. AND THE BOUNDARY WITH THE PROPHYLAXIS REVIEW: extended anticoagulation in patients who have ALREADY HAD a venous thromboembolism is TREATMENT and belongs here; primary prophylaxis in patients who have not is PREVENTION and belongs to the sibling. The discriminator is read from each trial's eligibility criteria, because the registry's coded `primaryPurpose` does not carry it and both conventions are used for both situations. Criteria are DERIVED POST HOC and say so.1

Each criterion above is recorded with the source it was derived from in `screening.eligibility_provenance`; none is asserted here without one.2

Methods — synthesis

For recurrent symptomatic venous thromboembolism -- nonfatal deep vein thrombosis or nonfatal pulmonary embolism -- with NO death term, a random-effects model was fitted with the REML estimator.1

Intervals are 95% confidence intervals.2

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials) (22 August 2019 version, as reproduced in the Cochrane Handbook), following Higgins JPT, Savovic J, Page MJ, Elbers RG, Sterne JAC. Chapter 8: Assessing risk of bias in a randomized trial. In: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5.1. A RESULT, not a study -- Handbook 8.2. Every judgement below names the outcome it is about, and for two of the three that outcome is a SECONDARY. 3 result-level assessments were made. A domain that cannot be judged from the registration and the posted results is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect.3

A ceiling applies to every risk-of-bias judgement in this review; it is stated with the assessment itself rather than summarised here.4

Certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE, following Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5.1, Chapter 14. HIGH for a body of randomised evidence, then rated down. 1 pooled outcome(s) were rated. No domain is rated up.5

Writing one now and calling it prespecified would invalidate every other refusal on this page, because a reader who caught it would be right to disbelieve all of them. Results

The pooled risk ratio for recurrent symptomatic venous thromboembolism -- nonfatal deep vein thrombosis or nonfatal pulmonary embolism -- with NO death term was 0.776 (0.344 to 1.75, 95% interval) across 3 trials, against another anticoagulant.1

Noted on this pool. Read this beside the estimate. Not one of the three contributing trials masks anybody: NCT03045406, NCT03266783 and NCT01780987 all register masking: none. The endpoint is adjudicated on all three, which is the standard mitigation for an open-label anticoagulation trial, but no registration states that the adjudicators were blinded. On NCT03266783 the registered primary is clinically relevant bleeding and recurrent VTE is the third of nine secondaries. On NCT01780987 the registered primary is major bleeding and recurrent VTE is the first of five. Only caravaggio contributes its own registered primary. Dalteparin, rivaroxaban, and unfractionated heparin followed by warfarin. The pooled quantity is therefore apixaban against whatever else was given, which is one step from any question a reader has. This object's GRADE rates indirectness down for it and the certainty here is very LOW.2

The trials' results were closely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 0%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 0, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 1.26, on degrees of freedom 2. computed; tau-squared is 0 and at k=3 that is an estimate from almost no information, which is why the interval is Knapp-Hartung on 2 degrees of freedom rather than a normal one3

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: Three trials randomise apixaban ITSELF against another anticoagulant for the acute event and post an arm-level count of recurrent symptomatic VTE with no death term. Their definitions were read and compared, not their names. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.4

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.5

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials). The unit of assessment is a result, not a study -- Handbook 8.2. Every judgement below names the outcome it is about, and for two of the three that outcome is a secondary.1

No result in this review can reach LOW risk of bias on the evidence we can reach, and that is a fact about our access rather than about the trials. Discussion

[Draft] The pooled RR is 0.776 (95% CI 0.344 to 1.753) over 3 trials. Certainty is rated VERY_LOW. Whether a change of that magnitude is clinically meaningful in this population is the author's judgement: no field on this object records a threshold of importance, and none is assumed here.1

[Draft] Across 3 trials, tau-squared 0; every trial interval includes no effect. Whether that degree of disagreement matters clinically -- whether the trials are answering the same question in the same patients -- is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] No published synthesis was appraised against this review, so no difference between this result and a published one is recorded. There is nothing here for this sentence to explain, and stating a reason for a difference that has not been established would be inventing one.3

[Draft] The evidence base is 3 trials, assessed for risk of bias as SOME_CONCERNS on 3 result(s). GRADE certainty is VERY_LOW. Whether that is enough to answer the question depends on the decision the answer is for, which is not stated on this object, and is the author's judgement.4

[Draft] primary trials. No bibliographic search for primary trials was run. The 4 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on the dates recorded on each entry. Whether that is broad enough for the claim this review makes is the author's judgement.5

[Draft] Certainty was not rated down on any GRADE domain. What further evidence would change the conclusion is a judgement about a trial nobody has run, and is the author's.6

Protocol status. Prespecified: False. A protocol specified before data collection is a historical fact about the past and cannot be created retrospectively. Writing one now and calling it prespecified would invalidate every other refusal on this page, because a reader who caught it would be right to disbelieve all of them.1

Eligibility criteria were derived post hoc when `apixaban-vte` was split in two on 2026-08-19, after the parent object's included set existed. The derivation is recorded element by element in `screening.eligibility`, and the criterion that separates this review from its sibling is stated in full at `screening.boundary_criterion`.2

Authority: Mecir R107 permits post-hoc eligibility criteria provided they are declared as such. They are declared, here and on the page.3

reconciliation82 surfaced = 54 experimental + 19 comparator + 7 background + 2 not-assessable; 80 of the 82 had a role located. 73 place apixaban in the randomised contrast and are this review's candidate pool. 1 was in the parent object and 72 were screened, so k_screened = 73. 48 excluded + 25 eligible = 73. Of the 25 eligible, 12 have posted no results, 2 are eligible and not poolable, and 11 are eligible and poolable. REMAINDER ZERO.
why_the_remainder_is_now_ZERO_and_was_71It was 71 when the split was recorded and the whole remainder has since been screened -- 39 excluded and 16 sent to adjudication mechanically, the 16 adjudicated by hand. A REMAINDER IS NOT A QUEUE TO BE DRAINED; screening it is what turned 71 into a disposition table, and the shape of that table is the finding: 48 of 73 fail a criterion, and 39 of the 48 fail on POPULATION -- 30 at the mechanical screen and all 9 of the adjudicated exclusions -- because they are thromboprophylaxis trials in patients who have never had a venous thromboembolism. The surfacing query reaches across the treatment/prevention boundary because ONE SEARCH OVER ONE DRUG NECESSARILY DOES; that is a fact about splitting a drug topic in two, not a criticism of the query, and the sibling review holds the trials this one excludes.
why_k_included_is_4_and_k_pooled_is_3The object holds RAMBLE (NCT02829957), which the parent included and which cannot contribute -- n=19, both arms typed ACTIVE_COMPARATOR, registered primary a pictorial menstrual blood-loss chart -- together with the three trials that pool. It is kept and named rather than dropped, because a trial that fails only at the POOLING step is a fact about this review's evidence base and dropping it would erase that fact. ELEVEN trials are eligible and poolable and only THREE contribute: the other eight post no arm-level count of the shared estimand, and each is named on the page.

The withholding question, asked at every rank

does each trial report a recurrent-VTE efficacy outcome at ANY registered rank -- primary, secondary or other -- before concluding which trials can be combined?

YES AT EVERY RANK, AND THE ANSWER DOES NOT SETTLE POOLABILITY

IT BOUGHT THE REVIEW ITS ENTIRE POOL. All three contributing results were found by asking at every rank: two of the three are SECONDARY outcomes in trials whose registered PRIMARY is a bleeding endpoint, so a review reading primaries only would have reported that they contribute nothing. IT DID NOT BUY POOLABILITY: eight trials answered yes and five of the eight still do not pool, each for a named reason. The prophylaxis half of this pair ran the identical discipline and its poolable set went 3 -> 8. HERE IT WENT 8 -> 3. THE METHOD HAS NO DIRECTION -- asking is not a way of finding more trials, it is a way of finding out.

The same question, the opposite answer

Table 17. The same question, the opposite answer
reviewpoolable setdirection
apixaban-vte-treatment8 -> 3DOWN -- the question DISSOLVED a pool
apixaban-vte-prophylaxis3 -> 8UP -- the question RECOVERED a pool

THE SAME QUESTION, ASKED THE SAME WAY, ON THE SAME DRUG, ON THE SAME NIGHT, MOVED ONE REVIEW'S POOLABLE SET UP AND THE OTHER'S DOWN. Every earlier instance in this corpus recovered a pool, and a check that has only ever returned the convenient answer cannot be told apart from no check at all. This pair is the refutation, and it arose on its own rather than being sought: it cost the treatment review the two largest trials in its field. Asking the withholding question is not a way of finding more trials. It is a way of finding out.

NOT that either pool is correct -- both were judged by reading endpoint definitions, and that judgement stands or falls on its own. NOT that the direction is unpredictable in general; two instances are two instances. What it establishes is narrow and it is the thing that was missing: THE PROCEDURE HAS NO BUILT-IN DIRECTION, demonstrated rather than asserted.

Published-meta comparison — PENDING_EXTERNAL_RESOLUTION

Denominator: —. Not established, and the obstacle is that no candidate synthesis has been identified for this estimand at all. The PubMed search at search.databases[2] reported 439 record(s) and retrieved 50; 389 were not retrieved and none of the 50 retrieved has been screened for whether it synthesises recurrent VTE on apixaban. There is therefore nothing yet to form a denominator over -- not a synthesis whose included set is unresolved, but no identified synthesis.

Explicitly not done: CITATION-STRING MATCHING. It would produce a comparison-shaped answer tonight and it is not identity: two syntheses citing the same trial under different labels would read as different, and the same label on different trials as the same. That is the substitution class this project audits for.
